utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning. General, the affirmation you made at the beginning of your evidence does still apply. Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. If we could look at Exhibit P75, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: General, if it would assist you to look at a hard copy. Actually, I don't have hard copies, so we could use the Macedonian version. Can we make the Macedonian version larger, please. General, on Tuesday, at page 3684 of the transcript, my colleague asked you about this document. It is the decision by Minister Boskoski to establish a special police unit. And on Tuesday, you explained that this document actually refers to the posebna unit which was created long before 2001. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And, General, I'll ask you, as always, try to speak up a little bit for the interpreters. In the Macedonian version, could we turn to the second page, please. And, General, I'd like you to focus on paragraph 6. It starts on the second page in the Macedonian version. It's on the bottom of the first page in the English version. Do you see paragraph 6 there, General?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see Item 6.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Item 6 says: "The commanding and basic composition of the Special Unit is provided from the Department for Police, SVR/Sector for Internal Affairs/of the city of Skopje, the sectors and departments of internal affairs in the Republic of Macedonia, that is, for each battalion, and the platoon for logistics individually." And then below that, we see the following: "The following number of members of police is provided for the Skopje battalion, from the Department for Police- 2." You see that, General?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: " ... From the Centre for Training Animals and Training - 10; from the Sector for Security, Police Station for the security of buildings of the government of the Republic of Macedonia and diplomatic-consular representation officers-49." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: So just to clarify, Item 6 shows that the posebna unit was made up of regular police as well as officers or personnel from other units such as the Ministry of Interior's Sector for Security and Protection; is that fair?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it might be said so.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And that Sector for Security and Protection, that's the unit that you described yesterday as the unit that provides security to high-level officials of the Macedonian government, as well as security and protection to government buildings; right?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and also the diplomatic and consular representative offices.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Yesterday at page 3813 of the transcript, my learned colleague asked you whether after your committee completed its work in September 2001, whether the government of Macedonia ever suggested that the work of that committee was somehow faked or that it was not a sincere effort to reveal the truth. And you replied: "No, the government adopted that information." Do you recall this exchange?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: So would it be fair to say, then, that Minister Boskoski also adopted the information provided by your committee?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we turn, please, to Exhibit P73. Your Honours, this is at tab 1 of the Prosecution's binder.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: General, this is again the decision of 13 August 2001, signed by Minister Boskoski, to establish the commission of which you were a member, and I'd like to ask you, please, could you focus on Part 2, because I'd like to ask your help with part of it. In the middle of Part 2, it says this: "The Commission from Item 1 of this decision has the task to review the circumstances and analyse the activities undertaken by the security forces of the Minister of Internal Affairs to repel the armed attacks of terrorist groups on 12/08/2001 in the village of Ljuboten- Skopje." Do you follow me?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I follow you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Just to clarify, did the mandate of this commission then include investigating the treatment of ethnic Albanian civilians who were stopped at check-points outside of the village of Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that it included everything related to Ljuboten.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. Then would the mandate of this commission have included investigating the treatment of ethnic Albanian residents of Ljuboten who were detained by the police on the 12th of August, 2001, and held in various police stations outside of Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course, it includes that as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Focusing on, then, this mandate to analyse the activities undertaken by the security forces of the Ministry of Internal Affairs in the village of Ljuboten, can we accept, General, that by the 13th of August, when he issued this decision, logically, then, Minister Boskoski was aware that certain security forces of the Ministry of the Interior had operated in Ljuboten on the 12th of August?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would not be able to confirm this.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Well, why, then, would the Minister have issued the decision that he issued?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because we received some information, I don't remember where it came from, whether it was representatives of the International Community or from the media, and that is a sufficient reason for the Minister to react in this way to make a decision to establish a commission.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: What was the information that you received from the International Community and the media between the 12th and 13th of August?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't be -- I couldn't remember very precisely, but I can summarise. I remember there were various information -- there was various information that there was some clashes between the citizens, that there was, I don't know, shelling by the police, which was not true because the police did not have such weapons available, such as strong weapons, with some number of killed civilians, five, ten, fifteen, I can't remember how many exactly. I know there were all sorts of information that I would call them disinformations or speculations.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Was information received indicating that security forces of the Ministry of the Interior were present in Ljuboten on the 12th of August?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The information that I was receiving from the very beginning and immediately after that was that our positions in the village of Ljuboten were attacked and that our security forces had returned to it. I had no other information about that at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: When you say "our security forces were attacked," do you mean the Ministry's security forces were attacked in Ljuboten; is that what you mean?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I say "our security forces," I'm thinking about the security forces, the army and the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Was Minister Boskoski accountable for the actions of the Ministry's security forces?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: You might say so, but not directly, because his commander heading was carried out by him through the two directors and the under-secretaries for criminal police and the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: The chain of command ran from the lower echelons to the higher echelons to Minister Boskoski?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That is the hierarchy which I thought I explained.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Yesterday, at page 3795 of the transcript, my colleague asked you: "Is it also correct that without exhumation and postmortem of the bodies, first you could not know how many people were killed, what was the status of those people, what killed those people, and under which circumstances they were killed?" And you responded: "It is correct, yes." Do you recall that exchange?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember, and I stand by that even now.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: General, if you wanted to know how many people were killed at Ljuboten, if someone wanted to know how many people were killed at Ljuboten, could they obtain that information from speaking with members of the Ministry of the Interior who were present in the village on the 12th of August?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that from my position of my official duties, I was not able to know that, that you should -- it would be correct to ask that question to my colleague Zivko Petrovski, who was in charge of the police department.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Well, let's speak hypothetically. I said if someone wanted to know how many people were killed at Ljuboten, would one way of obtaining that information be from speaking with members of the Ministry of the Interior who were present in the village on the 12th of August?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I -- we object to this line of questioning because this is a hypothetical question, but that is not the basic objection. My basic objection is that the Prosecutor is departing from the assumption that the witness has said that units of the Ministry of the Interior were in Ljuboten, but as far as I remember this statement was not given -- the witness didn't give at all during his days of evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I agree with what you say, but I don't think, in the end, that provides a valid basis for objection to this question, which is really putting just a simple proposition to the witness, whether or not speaking to members present on the 12th of August would have been one way of obtaining information about what occurred. Continue, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: General Galevski, if someone wanted to know how many people were killed at Ljuboten, would one way of obtaining that information be from speaking with persons who were present in the village of Ljuboten on the 12th of August?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably you are right, but we had a commander, we had a head, assistant minister and his deputies that we were in contact with. We have discussed on this topic, at least about the -- relating to the parts in the uniform. And I will repeat again, my direct subordinate for the city of Skopje and for that area was Mr. Ljupco Bliznakovski, who was on the field every day and who had contact with the Cair area, and if -- whenever -- if he would have received any precise information, I would have surely received it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: General, if you wanted to know -- if someone wanted to know the status of the persons who were killed at Ljuboten, whether they were civilians or combatants, could someone perhaps obtain that information by speaking with persons who were present in Ljuboten on the 12th of August?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I already responded to this. We all tried, using our lines of information, to know about it, and to be honest, after these events, I've never went to Ljuboten.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: General, is your response to my question, then, a "yes" or a "no"?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't confirm.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: General, if you wanted to know -- if someone wanted to know what killed the persons who died on the 12th of August in Ljuboten, could someone obtain that information by speaking with persons who were present in the village on the 12th of August?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this question has already been asked, and I think that the Prosecutor could have asked all these questions in his investigation [sic] in chief because he discussed this document with the witness previously.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Carry on, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can you answer my question, General?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could not be able to confirm.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: General, if someone wanted to know under which circumstances these persons were killed at Ljuboten, could someone obtain that information by speaking with persons who were present in Ljuboten on the 12th of August?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would give you the same answer. I cannot confirm.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Saxon. General, that concludes the questions that will be asked of you. We would thank you for the time that you've taken to be here in I would give you the same answer. I cannot confirm.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Saxon. General, that concludes the questions that will be asked of you. We would thank you for the time that you've taken to be here in The Hague and the assistance that you've given, and you may now of course return to your normal activities. So the Court Officer will now show you from the court. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, and I wish you all good.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, the next witness will be Mr. Betulla Qaili, and he will be led by Mr. Neuner.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Could you please read the affirmation on the card that's shown to you now.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Please sit down. Now, Mr. Neuner will ask you some questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness.

utterances.speaker: BETULLA QAILI
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Your name is Betulla Qaili?

utterances.speaker: BETULLA QAILI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And you're an ethnic Albanian?

utterances.speaker: BETULLA QAILI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: You were born in the village of Ljuboten and live in Skopje in Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: BETULLA QAILI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And in September 2005, you provided a statement to the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: BETULLA QAILI
utterances.text: That's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: If I can just ask the usher to give the statement to the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And in April of this year, you met in Skopje a male representative from the Registry who certified that statement. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BETULLA QAILI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And before coming here today, did you have the opportunity to read through it?

utterances.speaker: BETULLA QAILI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And are its contents accurate?

utterances.speaker: BETULLA QAILI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, according to Rule 92 bis, I would like to tender the certified statement of this witness, with the ERN N006-4276 to 4295 into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P383, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I want to briefly summarise the content of that statement. The witness, Betulla Qaili, is the brother of Atulla Qaili. During the events in Ljuboten in the time period 10 to 12 August 2001, the witness was in Skopje. On Sunday afternoon, 12th August, he learned that his brother, Atulla Qaili and other Ljuboten residents, had been arrested by Macedonian forces. From Monday, 13th of August, until 18th of August, 2001, the witness, sometimes together with other persons, inquired about the whereabouts of his missing brother, Atulla. He visited the police stations in Butel, Bit Pazar, Autokomanda, Karpos, Prolece, and Mirkovci. He did neither see his brother, Atulla Qaili, at these police stations, nor find his name on their list of persons detained recently. A policeman in Mirkovci police station found the name Abdullah Cajani on the list of detained persons there. The witness also went to Sutka Prison, but his brother's name was not on the list of prisoners recently detained there. On or about 14th of August, 2001, the witness and Imer, last name unknown, went to Skopje city hospital. A physician told them there that Atulla Qaili was at the hospital. When Imer asked to see Atulla in the city hospital, the physician responded that the police would not allow this. Later, that same physician called Imer to tell him that Atulla Qaili was not in Skopje city hospital. The next day, the parents of the witness visited the Skopje city hospital. They did not see Atulla Qaili there. On the list of the hospital they found the name Abdullah Cajani. Twice, the witness visited the morgue Butel 1. He was told there his brother is not on the morgue's list of dead persons delivered recently. During his second visit, he was allowed to inspect the corpses, among which he recognised the buddy of his brother. That same day, having completed the administrative procedure at the morgue, the witness received a permission to bury his brother. His brother was buried in Ljuboten. About two weeks after the burial, the witness's family was visited by a policeman and asked about his dead brother. Witness, I want to show you a document. The 65 ter number is 279.2. For the record, the ERN number is N001-7426. Do you see that on the screen on the right-hand side in front of you?

utterances.speaker: BETULLA QAILI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: The title of the document is "Permission for Burial." It dates from the 18th of August, 2001, and you refer in paragraph 28 of your statement to it. Which institution issued this permission?

utterances.speaker: BETULLA QAILI
utterances.text: Butel Burial Institution.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: There is a box on the original, and there's a handwriting directly above it, and it says there: "The burial will take place in Ljuboten village." When was Atulla Qaili buried in Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: BETULLA QAILI
utterances.text: The day I took him, this is the day that I buried him.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And this is the 18th of August, 2001?

utterances.speaker: BETULLA QAILI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: You undertook numerous steps to find the body of your brother. On your own initiative, you visited several police stations, the Sutka Prison. After days of searching, you were finally successful and found your brother. My question to you is: How would you describe the role of the Macedonian authorities and the support they gave you during the search for your brother?

utterances.speaker: BETULLA QAILI
utterances.text: They didn't give me any support. It was me that tried to find him, who entered in this burial company. I entered with my cousin in the cemetery, and I found him there. This is what I said in my statement as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Did you ever receive an official explanation from any authority in Macedonia of what had happened to your brother while he was in custody of the police after the 12th of August, 2001?

utterances.speaker: BETULLA QAILI
utterances.text: No, nothing. I have never received any document or information about his whereabouts. It is me that found him.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: No further questions at this point in time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Neuner. Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Qaili. My name is Guenal Mettraux, and together with Ms. Residovic, we appear on behalf of General Boskoski. I would like to ask you a few questions from the statements you made in your statement to the Office of the Prosecutor. You have told the Prosecutor, is that correct, that you went to the city hospital, Skopje, on the 14th of August; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BETULLA QAILI
utterances.text: I don't remember the date. When the war started in Ljuboten, two to three days later, constantly I was searching for him. I went to the hospital and they said he wasn't admitted to the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that correct also that you went to the city hospital with your relative, Mr. Imer Arifi; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BETULLA QAILI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And can you recall approximately, if you can, as time has passed, what day it was when you went to the hospital?

utterances.speaker: BETULLA QAILI
utterances.text: It was in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you explained to the Prosecutor that you and Imer called a doctor from the front desk of the hospital. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BETULLA QAILI
utterances.text: Imer called him on number 15. They spoke on the phone, and he told him that Atulla Qaili was not there.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: You have explained to the Prosecution that Imer called this number because he personally knew this doctor; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BETULLA QAILI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you told the Prosecution that you had been present during this phone conversation between Imer and the doctor?

utterances.speaker: BETULLA QAILI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you also explained to the Prosecution that you wished not to reveal the name of this doctor in order to protect him; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BETULLA QAILI
utterances.text: Yes, due -- I was concerned for his security.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you have explained to the Prosecution that during this telephone conversation, the doctor told Imer that Atulla was at the hospital, but that you could not see him because the police would not let you; is that what you told the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: BETULLA QAILI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then you explained to the Prosecution or you told the Prosecution that you returned to the village of Ljuboten; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BETULLA QAILI
utterances.text: I didn't return to Ljuboten. I returned to my house in Skopje.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I apologise. In Skopje. And you explained that later on your relative, your cousin, Imer, called you to indicate to you he had had another phone call with that same doctor; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BETULLA QAILI
utterances.text: Yes, at about 2200 hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And Imer, during that conversation, told you that the doctor had denied what he had told you earlier; namely, that Atulla had been at the hospital; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BETULLA QAILI
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you also told the Prosecutor that Imer had been told to come back the next day to the hospital; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BETULLA QAILI
utterances.text: I don't remember this.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that correct, Mr. Qaili, that this is not exactly the way things happened; you were not in fact present during that phone call, is that correct, the first phone call between Imer and the doctor?

utterances.speaker: BETULLA QAILI
utterances.text: I was downstairs waiting while they were speaking on the phone.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: In fact, Imer didn't do that phone call from the hospital but from his home; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BETULLA QAILI
utterances.text: While we were together, he spoke with him from the hospital. Afterwards, whether it was from his home or elsewhere, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But the original contact between Imer and the doctor, you were not present, sir; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BETULLA QAILI
utterances.text: I was downstairs there waiting. He was speaking on the phone.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And, in fact, the doctor never told Imer that the police would not let you have access to Atulla; is that true?

utterances.speaker: BETULLA QAILI
utterances.text: I was present there. I saw police all around the hospital, and it is true, what he said to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But is that correct that this phone call, Imer did it on his own from his home and only the next day did you and Imer go together to the hospital; is that the way things happened?

utterances.speaker: BETULLA QAILI
utterances.text: We were at the hospital that day, not the day after. He spoke with him on Extension 15, Imer spoke with a doctor through Extension 15.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown Rule 65 ter 1D495. It has an ERN 1D00-4483 to 4488. There is no Macedonian.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Qaili, what I'm about to read to you is a statement taken by the Office of the Prosecution from Imer Arifi, your cousin, on the 15th of September, 2005. If I may ask the Registry to go to the third page of that document. That would be 1D00-4485. So there is no Macedonian or Albanian version of this document, so I'll read the paragraph to you. It's a statement attributed to your cousin, Imer Arifi, and he says this to the Prosecution: "When I heard it, I started making all inquiries as well as other my and Atulla relatives did, to find where Atulla is. Then I remember that somebody mentioned we should also check whether he is not in hospital. I called from my home phone to Skopje Town Hospital and spoke with the Macedonian male doctor. The doctor replied to my question, whether Atulla Qaili is hospitalised there, without hesitation, 'Yes, Atulla is here.' But I could felt from his voice, that he is very afraid as talking to me." Is that correct, Mr. Qaili, that Imer actually had that conversation which you mentioned from his own home and not from the phone at Skopje hospital?

utterances.speaker: BETULLA QAILI
utterances.text: I don't know with whom he spoke from home, but as far as the hospital is concerned, I was there, I'm sure. As far as his home is concerned, I don't know. I was not there.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then he explains that he went to the hospital the next day. I will read the paragraph to you, Mr. Qaili. It's the next paragraph, paragraph 7: "On the next day morning, I went to Skopje Town Hospital together with Betulla Qaili, the brother of Atulla. We went there around 8.00 a.m., and from reception asked the employee about the extension of the doctor whom did I spoke yesterday about one patient. Further on I explained the employee that the doctor invited me to come today, provided me with more details about the patient health condition. But I did not say and the employee, the name of patient, as being Atulla Qaili. Nevertheless, I do not know whether the employee knew what doctor did I speak yesterday, but told me to dial extension number 15, and I immediately recognised by the voice the same doctor as I spoke to yesterday." So is that correct, Mr. Qaili, that the visit to the hospital with Imer took place the day after he had had that original conversation with the doctor who informed him that Atulla was at the hospital; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BETULLA QAILI
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then at paragraph 8, Imer says the following: "I explained the doctor that I am the person who was asking yesterday about Atulla Qaili's hospitalisation --"

utterances.speaker: BETULLA QAILI
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'm still reading from the statement of your cousin, Mr. Qaili. I will ask you a question afterwards. And he says: "I got advice to come to the morgue. The doctor recognised me and apologised, saying that it was a mistake, because when we talked together about Atulla Qaili, he meant by mistake another person. He did not say anything else and just put the phone down so I could not ask him other questions." Is that correct, sir, that Mr. Arifi did not suggest that the doctor told him during that conversation or in the prior conversation that the police would not let you see Atulla; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BETULLA QAILI
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then in paragraph 9 of the statement, he says that you left the hospital, and I would like to ask the Registry to go to paragraph 12 of this statement. That's the next page. It's again the same statement, Mr. Qaili, and it's a different paragraph. This is what Imer said about the doctor in question, the doctor to whom he talked: "Being asked if I know the name of the doctor in Skopje Town Hospital, I say I do not know and it was the first time in my life I spoke to this person." Is that correct, Mr. Qaili, that in fact Imer did not know the doctor in question?

utterances.speaker: BETULLA QAILI
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Sir, you've explained to the Prosecution and to the Trial Chamber that you made a number of efforts and attempts to locate your brother, Atulla, and I would like to ask you a few questions about that. You recall mentioning to the Prosecution that sometimes after you had recovered the body of your brother, three policemen came to your house to ask you questions and ask you for documents about your brother, Atulla; do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: BETULLA QAILI
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct, but I was not there. I was at work. They asked my wife. My wife told them that I was at work, and they left.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is that correct that three or so days later, they came back to see you and ask you for information and documentation about your brother?

utterances.speaker: BETULLA QAILI
utterances.text: I don't remember whether they came after three days or not. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But can you remember, sir, that they indeed came back shortly after to ask you for that information?

utterances.speaker: BETULLA QAILI
utterances.text: They were once, but I don't remember when they came again. First they met with my wife, but I don't remember when they came for the second time. A lot of time has passed from then.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown P383. That's the statement of the witness that's just been admitted. And if I could ask the Registry to go to page 8 of the document, please. This would be -- for the Registry, this would be paragraph 36, and in the Albanian version as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Qaili, I will read a number of paragraphs from your statement which you gave to the Prosecution. It will appear on your screen as well. Paragraph 36, you were recorded as saying the following: "10, 15 days later, after burial of my brother, Atulla, three policemen came to my house and asking my wife whether I'm at home. My wife explained them that I am working and I'm not at home. They did not say why they were looking for me and just left." Do you recall that, Mr. Qaili?

utterances.speaker: BETULLA QAILI
utterances.text: They told her something about the documents, because I requested the ID, the driving permit, I asked the police about these documents, and they came to inquire whether we had found them or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then at paragraph 37 of your statement, you are recorded as saying the following: "Three days later again three policemen in uniforms came to my house, asking me if I have some personal documents of my brother Atulla or if I have any photos from his burial in Ljuboten." Do you recall saying that to the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: BETULLA QAILI
utterances.text: I had photos, but I didn't give them for security reasons. I did have photos.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And in fact you explained that you did not give them those pictures, but instead told them that you did not possess those pictures and documents; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BETULLA QAILI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And your concern at the time was that if you were to give them those documents, they might destroy them; is that the reason why you did not give them those documents?

utterances.speaker: BETULLA QAILI
utterances.text: For security concerns, this is why I didn't give the photos to the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And by "security concerns," Mr. Qaili, do you mean to say that you were concerned that they would destroy or make those pictures disappear or is that something else?

utterances.speaker: BETULLA QAILI
utterances.text: They could do anything. They could even take me to prison. This is the reason why I didn't give these photos.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that correct that after you had told them you did not possess any of those pictures or documents, the three policemen just left; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BETULLA QAILI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that fair to say also, Mr. Qaili, that at the time you did not trust the Macedonian police?

utterances.speaker: BETULLA QAILI
utterances.text: Not only at that time; even today I do not trust the Macedonian police.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is it fair to say that you understood at the time that if you were to give them those pictures, they may not use it for the purpose of investigating what happened to your brother?

utterances.speaker: BETULLA QAILI
utterances.text: I am sure they wouldn't take any action, they would just tear them, and nothing would have been done.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Now, are you aware, Mr. Qaili, that the police in fact made a number of efforts to try to establish the identity of your brother? Are you aware of those efforts?

utterances.speaker: BETULLA QAILI
utterances.text: No. I'm sure they didn't do anything. If they had done something, he had all his personal documents. They certainly wouldn't have taken him to the morgue without a name and -- a family name.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And are you aware that the police actually sought and obtained information that allowed them to identify your brother; is that something you are aware of?

utterances.speaker: BETULLA QAILI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'll simply give the numbers of the document for the transcript. It's 1D69.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Are you aware, Mr. Qaili -- It's an exhibit, I apologise, Exhibit 1D69. Are you aware, Mr. Qaili, that the police also carried out a papillary line test on the hand of your brother who had identified him; are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: BETULLA QAILI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Are you aware of the fact that the result of this test was then compared to documentations which the police had obtained which allowed them to identify your brother as Atulla Qaili; are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: BETULLA QAILI
utterances.text: I don't know. When I went to the morgue, I found him, and he had no identity. It's me that gave his name. The morgue gave me this document, and then I buried him.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, simply for the record, it's Exhibit 1D70 and 1D68.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Are you aware, Mr. Qaili, that an autopsy had been performed on your brother Atulla by the Forensic Institute in Skopje after his death?

utterances.speaker: BETULLA QAILI
utterances.text: No, I am not. I know only that an autopsy was performed on him after six months, but not before.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Were you aware that shortly after his death, this autopsy was carried out by the Forensic Institute to determine the cause and circumstances of his death? Is that information you had in your possession at the time?

utterances.speaker: BETULLA QAILI
utterances.text: No, I didn't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, for the record, it's Exhibit P49, among other documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Are you aware, sir, that the result of the autopsy at that time were then sent to the competent investigative judge in Skopje; is that information you possessed at the time?

utterances.speaker: BETULLA QAILI
utterances.text: Can you repeat the question, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I apologise. Are you or were you aware at the time that the result of the autopsy that was carried out on your brother Atulla were sent to the investigative judge in Skopje?

utterances.speaker: BETULLA QAILI
utterances.text: No, I'm not.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: For the record, it will be the transcript of these proceedings 19th of June, 2007, page 2342, and 20 June 2007, page 2408.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Were you aware at the time, Mr. Qaili, that the investigative judge had made requests for information to the forensic experts who had carried out the autopsy?

utterances.speaker: BETULLA QAILI
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Were you aware at the time that the autopsy report of Atulla and the court medical file of your brother were both provided to the investigative judge?

utterances.speaker: BETULLA QAILI
utterances.text: I don't know what they did. I know what I did, personally.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So am I correct to understand that you were not aware that this report, the autopsy report and the --

utterances.speaker: BETULLA QAILI
utterances.text: I didn't know anything about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Did you know that the competent investigative judge had visited the Forensic Institute in Skopje to make inquiries about your brother; did you know that?

utterances.speaker: BETULLA QAILI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, it would be P54, N001-9699-80-001. It's Exhibit P54.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Were you aware, Mr. Qaili, that the investigative judge also visited the Skopje city hospital at the time to collect information about your brother?

utterances.speaker: BETULLA QAILI
utterances.text: No, I was not.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you know that the public prosecutor of Skopje in fact issued an order to carry out an autopsy on your brother Atulla; were you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: BETULLA QAILI
utterances.text: No, I wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is P54 and P59.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Were you aware of the fact, Mr. Qaili, that the Ministry of Interior had in fact supported the suggestion of an autopsy for your brother; were you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: BETULLA QAILI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's 1D33.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Were you aware also that a request to the competent investigative judge had been made by the public prosecutor to investigate the circumstances of the death of your brother; were you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: BETULLA QAILI
utterances.text: No, no, I wasn't aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown, Your Honour, 1D227. It has an ERN 1D00-2452, and again it has neither an Albanian or Macedonian translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Qaili, this is the Prosecution's statement of a person called Jovan Serafimovski, who is a public prosecutor, and I'll read a paragraph to you. There is no Albanian version of this document. If the Registry could go to the third page of that document at paragraph 7, please. Mr. Qaili, I will read a number of sentences from the statement of that person, and then I'll ask you a question about it. This is what

utterances.speaker: MR. SERAFIMOVSKI SAID
utterances.text: "In the request to conduct an investigation submitted on 14 August 2001, the name of Qani, Atulla is mentioned. It was my obligation to ascertain the cause of death. I asked the investigative judge, Velce Pancevski, to inquire about this. We found out that Qani, Atulla was injured during a clash with the police and the army in Ljuboten." Were you aware, sir, that such a request had been made by Mr. Serafimovski to Mr. Pancevski?

utterances.speaker: BETULLA QAILI
utterances.text: I don't know, but that is not true about my brother having fought with the police. I don't know anything. I know that there were fighting in Ljuboten. I know simply that my brother was taken in the basement and then he got lost.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. Qaili, I think it might have been due to the translation. The statement of the persons that they found, not fought, simply that they had found your brother at the hospital. Were you aware, Mr. Qaili, that after the investigative judge had obtained this information, criminal charges that had been raised against your brother were dropped; were you aware of that fact?

utterances.speaker: BETULLA QAILI
utterances.text: I don't know anything about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is Exhibit P46.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Qaili, were you aware that in the weeks and months following the incident, the police sought to obtain information about the deceased from villagers; are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: BETULLA QAILI
utterances.text: No, I wasn't aware of that. I don't know anything about the police having inquired about him. I only know about my own efforts. The police never did anything to find out whether he was dead or alive. I only know that when I inquired about him in the police, they said, "He's not here."

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Are you aware of the fact, Mr. Qaili, that the police actually approached one village leader from Ljuboten, asking him to approach the families of the deceased for information; are you aware of that fact?

utterances.speaker: BETULLA QAILI
utterances.text: No. That is not true. I don't know anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you know someone called Kenan Saliu or Kenan Salievski; do you know about him?

utterances.speaker: BETULLA QAILI
utterances.text: I do, yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is that correct that he's one of the village leader in Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: BETULLA QAILI
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Did Mr. Saliu or Salievski ever ask you to provide information about your brother to the police?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Please ask the witness to speak slowly when he makes longer sentences and articulate better.

utterances.speaker: BETULLA QAILI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Qaili, we're being asked to speak a bit more clearly or more loudly, if you can. Perhaps it's the microphones that are too far from you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is Exhibit P104.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Qaili, you've also indicated that your brother was exhumed, I understand, sometime in the year 2002. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: BETULLA QAILI
utterances.text: When the autopsy was performed, when they exhumed him, I don't know whether it was after three months or six months, all of them were exhumed and they were -- performed an autopsy on them. And this is the only thing I know and I have said. All the world knows about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Now, are you aware of the fact that the request for exhumation and autopsy had come from the investigative judge; are you aware of that fact?

utterances.speaker: BETULLA QAILI
utterances.text: No, I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is inter alia P49, transcript of 20 June 2007, page 2393.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Qaili, I have only a few more questions. Is that correct that the name Cajani as appeared on some medical records is the name -- or the family name of your in-laws; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BETULLA QAILI
utterances.text: No, no. The name of my wife -- that is the last name of my wife, Cajani.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Yes, that was my question. Is that correct that it is the family name of the family of your wife; is that true?

utterances.speaker: BETULLA QAILI
utterances.text: Yes, of my in-laws.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if you can help with this, were you aware of the fact that the wife of your brother Atulla had left the village of Ljuboten on Friday, the 10th of August; are you aware of that fact?

utterances.speaker: BETULLA QAILI
utterances.text: Not on the 10th, but on the 11th of August. It was Saturday, the evening of Saturday, and they came straight to my home.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Qaili, thank you for your patience. Your Honour, that's all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Zivkovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Qaili, good afternoon. My name is Jasmina Zivkovic, and together with Mr. Apostolski, we represent Mr. Johan Tarculovski. I am sorry. I had some problems with my headphones. Mr. Qaili, in Ljuboten from 10th to 12th of August you were in Skopje; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BETULLA QAILI
utterances.text: Yes. I live in Skopje.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: And you didn't know what exactly happened in Ljuboten from 10th and 12th of August, with the exception of what you heard from your neighbours in Skopje; is this correct?

utterances.speaker: BETULLA QAILI
utterances.text: Yes, but we could see the smoke and the flame rising out of the village. You could see that from Skopje. But I wasn't there myself, that's true.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: You neither know where your brother Atulla was during the events in Ljuboten, you know only what the others told you?

utterances.speaker: BETULLA QAILI
utterances.text: He was at home. I'm certain that he was at home. My other brother was there. Everybody was there.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: But you weren't there, and you cannot confirm this?

utterances.speaker: BETULLA QAILI
utterances.text: I wasn't there, but my other brother, who is still alive, can testify to that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: All right. As you said to my learned colleague, you know that he started with the other villagers, but on half way he changed his mind and he climbed off of the tractor?

utterances.speaker: BETULLA QAILI
utterances.text: No, I didn't -- I didn't say that, never did I mention that he started to leave, but he was taken by the police in the basement along with some eight or ten other people. The others are still alive, whereas he disappeared.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: But his wife said that he descended the tractor and to stay home; is this correct?

utterances.speaker: BETULLA QAILI
utterances.text: I wasn't there. I don't know that he got on the tractor or not. I already stated that I was not at the village, and I am repeating it. I was not in the village.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Qaili. I don't have any more questions. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Neuner.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: First of all, I want to ask that the permission to burial, which I've shown to this witness during the examination-in-chief, is tendered into evidence. The 65 ter number was 279.2. The ERN was N001-7426.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. We don't really have an objection to the document being tendered and admitted, Your Honour. We would simply wish to know what the purpose of the tendering of the document is, and in particular whether the Prosecution seeks to rely to any of the information contained in this document as being accurate, because there seems to be an inaccuracy as relate to the date of the death of Mr. Qaili. We would simply seek a clarification from the Prosecution in relation to this matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, only if Mr. Neuner wants to give it, because it was a document you introduced, you understand. Yes, Mr. Neuner.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I don't have the paragraph now in front of me, but Betulla Qaili has dealt in his own statement with the date itself. The statement has been admitted by Your Honours, and I will be probably on one of the other days in a position to submit the exact paragraph of his statement. I can also ask the witness. As far as I know, he has received several documents, had compared the date --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Are you pursuing the question of date of death?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Yes. My learned friend had mentioned that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: And are you pursuing it just to have clarified whether the exhibit is accurate or are you pursuing it on the basis that the exhibit is accurate and any other evidence is wrong?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I would -- my submission would be that the permission of burial, the fact that this was issued as such, is accurate. Whether the information contained therein might differ from other evidence which is on the Prosecution's -- among the Prosecution's exhibits is another question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Mettraux, you can take it that Mr. Neuner is not advancing the content of the document as necessarily accurate.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Simply for the record, Your Honour, we didn't use this document. This is a document that was used by the Prosecution. And also for the record, there was no challenge to the -- there was no challenge to the actual date of the death of Mr. Qaili through Mr. -- Dr. Jacovski, and yesterday I believe Mr. Saxon also at page 66 pointed out the date of the death being the 13th of August.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That was my error. I'm sorry for that, Mr. Mettraux. Does this matter arise out of cross-examination, then, Mr. Neuner?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour. If you could please explain again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Did you merely forget to tender this?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, then we'll receive it as an act of goodwill.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will be received as Exhibit P384, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I have just one question, Mr. Qaili.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: You were asked about Abdullah Cajani or about the name Cajani. To the best of your recollection, does the person Abdullah Cajani exist in Ljuboten village?

utterances.speaker: BETULLA QAILI
utterances.text: In Ljuboten village, there are many families, five or six families. Each of them has its own last name. There is a family by this last name of Cajani, but there is not such a name of Abdullah Cajani, at least for the last 20 years. Before 20 years, I don't -- for people over 20 years, no. But for younger people, maybe, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: The Prosecution has no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Qaili, that concludes the questions that are to be asked of you. The Chamber is grateful that you have been able to come to The Hague and for the assistance that you've been able to give. We realise that the loss of your brother in this way is very disturbing to you. You are now able to return to your home and your family. The Court Officer will show you out. Thank you indeed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Prosecution has no further witnesses to call at this time. However, the Prosecution does have another matter to raise with the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, on the 30th of March, 2007, the Prosecution -- excuse me, the Trial Chamber issued its -- well, I have to actually ask the Chamber to go into private session, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. The Chamber has received six statements pursuant to Rules 92 bis for two of them and 92 ter for four of them, in accordance with earlier decisions, and Mr. Saxon will now briefly summarise their content. The tapes will last six minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Then I better speak quickly. The witness Kire Ruseski, Your Honour, the written witness statement, will testify -- the statement refers to the duty and powers of the accused Ljube Boskoski as Minister of the Interior in 2001 to initiate investigations into the use of fire-arms by the Macedonian police. He will testify to the role of the head of the Professional Standards Unit and the duty of that head of the Professional Standards Unit to report to the Minister of the Interior. Your Honour, the statement of Ramus Jashari describes the attack on Ljuboten during the weekend of 10 to 12 August, 2001, the gunfire and shelling that had begun previously on the morning of 10th August 2001, the intensifying of gunfire and shelling on the morning of the morning of 12 August 2001, beginning at approximately 8.00 to 8.30 a.m., and the fact that the witness did not see anyone in Ljuboten village providing armed resistance to the Macedonian security forces participating in the attack. The witness also refers to the destruction of homes of several persons in the village, including his own home and the home of Afet Jashari which were burned. Your Honour, witness Marie von Baltenau testified to statements provided by 25 Ljuboten residents, ethnic Albanian Ljuboten residents, to members of the OSCE following their release from prison in Macedonia in December 2001. These 25 statements describe the murder and cruel treatment of Ljuboten residents both during the attack on the village on 12 August 2001, and subsequently in places of detention in and around Ljuboten, as well as in the city of Skopje. Your Honours, witness Dragoljub Cakic was a deputy public prosecutor at Basic Court II in Skopje at the time of the crimes charged in the amended indictment, and his statement describes Mr. Cakic's judicial activities in relation to the circumstances and events arising in and out of the attack on Ljuboten on 10 to 12 August 2001. Your Honours, the statement of witness Muzafer Jusufovski describes how he was at home on Sunday, the 12th of August, in the village of Ljuboten. He was actually at the home of his cousin, Elmaz Jusufi on that morning, and the witness heard a loud noise at the gate of the Jusufi home followed by gunfire. The witness saw police officers in various uniforms in the yard. The witness heard the door to the house being thrown open and then the police fired their weapons into the Jusufi home. And finally, Your Honours, the written statement of Mr. Jorgen Engel describes Mr. Engel's work as the head of the office and permanent and resident representative of the International Management Group in Skopje, and the witness will describe -- the witness's statement will describe the wanton destruction of homes and property in Ljuboten, and the statement also describes the work of the International Management Group in the process of reconstruction and rehabilitation in the conflict-affected areas of Macedonia, including reconstruction and repairs to damaged homes in Ljuboten. I believe I've addressed each of the six witnesses, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Saxon, and consecutive numbers will be given to those. I anticipate they'll be Exhibits P385 to P390, but we leave you to liaise finally with the Registry Officer in the court to ensure that occurs.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The Chamber now adjourns for the court vacation. It resumes on the afternoon of Tuesday, the 21st of August, and we will no doubt be able to then to proceed with the evidence at a pace which we believe will need to be quickened from the pace that we have been maintaining until now. The tendering of these statements today should enable the Chamber to issue the last decision of the various motions that have been before the Chamber, other motions having been dealt with by decisions of yesterday and today. We hope that you will all be refreshed from the vacation, and we adjourn at this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: 10.36 a.m., to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 21st day of August, 2007, at 2.15 p.m.
